# pass Provider

Reads and writes secrets in a shared, git-backed [pass](https://www.passwordstore.org/)
password store. Secrets are GPG-encrypted files in pass format; the store is a git
repository shared with humans using the `pass` (or [gopass](https://www.gopass.pw/))
CLI, and the provider stays byte-compatible with what those tools read and write.

Point the provider at the store's git URL with `repo_url`. It maintains its own
clone in a per-repository cache (`~/.cache/terraform-provider-pass/`), updates it
when the provider configures, and wraps every write in a safe sync: fetch, rebase
onto the remote branch, commit, push (retrying rejected pushes up to 3 times).
Conflicting concurrent writes to the same secret fail loudly; the provider never
auto-resolves them.

Alternatively, point `store_dir` at a checkout you manage yourself. Exactly one of
`repo_url` and `store_dir` must be set.

## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "pass" {
  repo_url = "git@github.com:example-org/passwords.git"
}

resource "pass_password" "db" {
  path     = "Utvikling/Azure/db_password"
  password = "correct-horse-battery"
  data = {
    username = "app_user"
  }
}

data "pass_password" "db" {
  path = pass_password.db.path
}
```

## Requirements

- `git` and `gpg` binaries on `PATH`, with a GPG key that can decrypt the store.
- Access to the store's git remote (e.g. an SSH key for `repo_url`).
- A git identity: commits are created with the operator's `user.name` /
  `user.email` and follow the operator's signing configuration. **CI jobs must
  configure a git identity** or every write fails with git's
  "Please tell me who you are" error.

## Migrating from 1.x

1.x could not clone the store itself, so a common workaround was materializing
the store through a Terraform module checkout:

```terraform
# 1.x workaround — remove this
module "dppasswords" {
  source = "git@github.com:example-org/passwords.git"
}

provider "pass" {
  store_dir = ".terraform/modules/dppasswords"
}
```

Module checkouts are on a detached HEAD, which 2.0 rejects at configure time
(1.x accepted them, then every write failed mid-apply with
`the destination you provided is not a full refname`). Replace the module with
`repo_url` and delete the module block:

```terraform
# 2.0
provider "pass" {
  repo_url = "git@github.com:example-org/passwords.git"
}
```

Also note in 2.0:

- Exactly one of `repo_url` and `store_dir` must be set (`store_dir` still
  falls back to `$PASSWORD_STORE_DIR`).
- `store_dir` with the default `refresh_store = true` must be a git clone with
  an `origin` remote; set `refresh_store = false` for purely local stores.
- The data source attributes are now sensitive: outputs referencing them must
  be declared `sensitive = true`.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `branch` (String) Branch of `repo_url` to read and write. Defaults to the remote HEAD branch.
- `refresh_store` (Boolean) Whether to update the store from its git remote when the provider configures (fetch + reset for `repo_url` store caches, fetch + rebase for a `store_dir` clone). With `false` the provider works offline from the existing checkout: reads may be stale, but writes still push.
- `repo_url` (String) Git URL of the password store repository (e.g. `git@github.com:org/passwords.git`). The provider maintains its own clone of it in a per-repository store cache and pushes every write. Exactly one of `repo_url` and `store_dir` must be set.
- `store_dir` (String) Existing local password store directory to use, e.g. a clone you manage yourself. Defaults to `$PASSWORD_STORE_DIR`. Must be checked out on a branch (not a detached HEAD); prefer `repo_url` and let the provider manage the checkout. Exactly one of `repo_url` and `store_dir` must be set.
